From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook, compared with the Seller's update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble

The Seller says its positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL" and are "not intended to be re-opened." It also calls 10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers "market standard."

- **Treat these statements as advocacy, not agreement.** They come from the other side's draft.
- **No authority exists for the fallbacks.** Our playbook records that Amelia Frost has given no written authority for the 20% cap or the 18-month period, for this draft or any other.
- **Recommendation:** Do not treat any position as agreed. Ask the Seller in writing to identify any document it says records principal-level agreement. Separately, confirm the position internally with Amelia Frost.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once it is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis.** The Seller's figures are five times ours, and the deductible structure removes the first AUD 250k of every recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. It also proposes that every limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject both elements. Restore 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** The 18-month fallback has no Amelia Frost approval, and the default would quietly pull Title, Tax, fraud and indemnity claims into the general limit.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so they cannot be capped at 20% or time-barred at 18 months.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature," which would cover fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps and baskets;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy;
  - non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and insert an express carve-out. This point is non-negotiable.** The playbook says no one may waive it, and an "all Claims" formulation is an attempt to limit fraud liability.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 22 Sep 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Accept only specific disclosures that are fairly and clearly described.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would turn every document into a warranty exception.
- **Related point:** Add a drafting point on DL 1.4, which denies any admission. That is acceptable as long as it does not dilute the effect of the specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must:
  - be tied to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** Its "discoverable" and "advisers" wording would effectively void the warranties for anything our diligence could have found.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the consent treated as satisfied once Bluefen's written consent is delivered (cl 3/6.3).
- **Facts disclosed (DL 2):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of revenue, roughly 30%. No final consent has been provided, and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring both an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective, unconditional consent plus evidence of 11.3 satisfaction a condition precedent.** Reasonable endeavours plus consent-on-delivery is not enough for a customer that represents about 30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release to be provided after Completion. About AUD 3.2m is outstanding (cl 2/7).
- **Facts disclosed (DL 3):** The facility has not been repaid, and no discharge of security has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require a payout letter, direct payment from the funds flow, and executed releases (including PPSR) at Completion.** A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Facts disclosed (DL 5):** The disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item, or expressly Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion. Add a line item, or a specific Seller indemnity and treatment as Debt/price adjustment, covering the bonuses plus on-costs.** Otherwise the Company bears the liability after Completion and the Buyer pays for it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity (cl 11.1) is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Facts disclosed (DL 4):** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee has cleared. No receipt or confirmatory assignment has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering the IP ownership gap, with the SOW3 cure preserved.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of IP to vest. Require payment plus a confirmatory assignment as the cure.**
- **Valuation caution:** DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but that figure has not been independently verified in either direction. Do not adopt it as the measure of exposure, and do not treat it as confirmed unpaid.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Facts disclosed (DL 6):** A download link was sent to an unintended external address and may contain about 1,240 records. The following are not established:
  - whether anyone accessed the file;
  - the exact scope;
  - whether notification is required.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - a proper investigation;
  - regular updates.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation and add the following:**
  - covenants to preserve logs, investigate and provide updates before Completion;
  - a warranty on completeness of the incident disclosure;
  - a specific indemnity for consequences of the incident.
- **Framing caution:** Do not frame our position as though a breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss is confirmed, because none is.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Facts disclosed (DL 8):** The disclosure is silent on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of each renewal, with no automatic treatment as Debt and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" yet. Request DD-008/DD-011 analysis covering the following, then decide on treatment:**
  - timing;
  - related-party character;
  - termination rights;
  - accrual status.

  Neither side's label should be assumed before the facts are tested.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims (cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5). Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept in separate categories, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the global application. Add express carve-outs so each category has its own regime.** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" default reverses the burden and overrides every specific regime by default.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Facts disclosed (DL 10):** The Seller itself says this does not mean the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof. Require the following:**
  - an ASIC extract;
  - PPSR searches;
  - original share certificates;
  - board and shareholder authorisations;
  - an encumbrance release and confirmation.

  An internally maintained register is a source the Seller supplied, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** The tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain open. No unlimited liability and no resolution should be assumed.
- **Recommendation:** **Record Tax and IP as open in the issues list and reserve our position.** The Seller cannot declare open terms settled by putting them under a regime we have rejected.

---

## Summary and next steps

**Positions to reject:**
- **Fallback-only positions:** the cap and time-limit offers match fallbacks we have no authority to use.
- **Below playbook:** the thresholds, the Bluefen consent mechanics and the bonus treatment.

**Positions we cannot concede:**
- the fraud carve-out (SPA-N-005);
- the Fundamental/Title regime (SPA-N-004);
- deletion of the buyer-knowledge exclusion (SPA-N-007).

**Positions that need evidence or investigation:**
- Bluefen consent (SPA-N-008);
- Riverlark payout and releases (SPA-N-009);
- Title evidence (SPA-N-015);
- Ironquay IP (SPA-N-011);
- the DD-006 incident (SPA-N-012);
- the Sandbar renewals (SPA-N-013).

**Recommended next steps:**
1. Send a mark-up restoring the playbook positions.
2. Send a written response rejecting the "FINAL / settled at principal level" characterisation.
3. Escalate internally to Amelia Frost only if the deal team wants to consider the cap or time-limit fallbacks. Any authority must be in writing and must identify the draft.
